'''Eleanor Elizabeth Bryce Campbell''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|FInstP]] (born 13 April 1960) is a Scottish scientist who held the Chair of Chemistry at the [[University of Edinburgh]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chem.ed.ac.uk/staff/academic-staff/professor-eleanor-e-b-campbell-frs|title=Professor Eleanor E. B. Campbell FRS {{!}} School of Chemistry|website=www.chem.ed.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2017-12-26}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite book|title=Who's who|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2010|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.251235}}</ref>

==Education==
Campbell was born in 1960 in [[Rothesay, Bute|Rothesay]] on the [[Isle of Bute]] in [[Scotland]] to Isobel and William Cowan.<ref name=":1" /> She was schooled at [[Rothesay Academy]] before going on to study for a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in [[Chemical Physics]] at the [[ University of Edinburgh]], passing with first class honours in 1982. She remained at the university for further 4 years studying for a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]], which she gained in 1986,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bryce|first=Campbell, Eleanor Elizabeth|date=1986|title=Electronic and vibrational excitation in atom / molecule collisions|hdl=1842/13295|language=en}}</ref> on the topic of ''Electronic to rovibrational excitation in fast atom-molecule collisions''.<ref>{{cite news|title=Academy graduate joins Royal Society |url=http://www.buteman.co.uk/news/local-headlines/academy-graduate-joins-royal-society-1-369496 |work=The Buteman |date=23 June 2010 |access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.research.ed.ac.uk/portal/en/persons/eleanor-eb-campbell(8dbfe83c-c8d3-45f0-b9c0-8ab19cf60049).html|title=Eleanor E.B. Campbell - Edinburgh Research Explorer|website=www.research.ed.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2017-12-26}}</ref> She then went to the [[University of Freiburg]] having received a [[habilitation]] in [[experimental physics]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Biography of Eleanor Campbell on University of Edinburgh website|url=http://www.ecampbell.chem.ed.ac.uk/group-members/eleanor-campbell}}</ref>

==Academic career==
After her time as assistant professor at the University of Freiburg, Campbell became a departmental head at the Max-Born Institut in 1993. In 1998 she was made Chair of Atomic and Molecular Physics at [[University of Gothenburg]], Sweden, before returning to the University of Edinburgh in to take up a post as Chair of Physical Chemistry in 2007 and then Chair of Chemistry 2013.<ref name=":0" />

Campbell was elected as a Foreign Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] (physics class) in 2005<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kva.se/en/contact/Kontakt-sida/?personId=3381|title=Kungliga Vetenskapsakademien - Contact Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences|website=www.kva.se|access-date=2016-06-30|archive-date=13 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013170654/http://www.kva.se/en/contact/Kontakt-sida/?personId=3381|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/807_RSEFellows.html|title=The Royal Society of Edinburgh {{!}} RSE Fellows|website=www.royalsoced.org.uk|access-date=2016-06-30}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In 2010 she was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] for her contribution to the understanding of relaxation channels and reorganisational dynamics of highly excited molecules and surfaces through experimental research.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/eleanor-campbell-11183/|title=Royal Society - Eleanor Campbell webpage}}</ref> She was made a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] and a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] in 2008.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/Membership/Networking/InterestGroups/FaradayDivision/FDCouncil.asp|title=Faraday Division Council Members|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|access-date=2017-12-26}}</ref> In 2018 she was elected as a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Campbell_Eleanor|title=Academia Europaea: Eleanor Campbell|access-date=4 November 2023}}</ref>

Campbell retired in the summer of 2025 and became Professors Emeritus at the University of Edinburgh, School of Chemistry.

== Current work ==
Campbell's group at the University of Edinburgh study the fundamental ionisation mechanisms and excited state dynamics of complex molecules in the gas phase using femtosecond laser spectroscopy. They also study carbon nanomaterials and develop microporous carbon-based materials for gas capture and storage.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ecampbell.chem.ed.ac.uk/|title=Eleanor Campbell Group {{!}} Eleanor Campbell site|website=www.ecampbell.chem.ed.ac.uk|access-date=2016-06-30|archive-date=17 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617002551/http://www.ecampbell.chem.ed.ac.uk/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
